about: Pre-registered predictions: the app's renders of takes not yet recorded (tests/predictions/PREDICTIONS.md).

tolerances.clipNote: Share of a segment's samples within 10% (0.9 dB) of the clamp, in percentage points; tested where either side is over 0.5%. 10% rather than 5% because game sound riding on clipped stretches pushes samples out of a narrower window: stand-in takes (--simulate-takes: a render plus the game sound of a real take, so the model is exact) lost up to 6 points at 5%.
tolerances.levelNote: Levels are measured in each segment's band (reference.js segmentBand: 30 Hz either side of a steady tone or 1 kHz sine, 150 Hz-10 kHz for noise, sweeps, clicks and the vowel) over its middle 60%. A segment predicted at least scorableAboveAmbienceDb over the take's ambience in that band (median of its quiet segments of 1 s or more) must come within levelDb. One predicted lower passes if the take is below that line plus levelDb (the ambience adds to it).
tolerances.holdsNote: A hypothesis holds for a take if at least segmentShare of its scored segments are within tolerance, at most bandsMissed spectrum bands are not, and the clamp is within ceilingDb.
tolerances.decisiveNote: Between two hypotheses, the discriminating segments are those where no measurement can pass both: level predictions more than twice levelDb apart, or one predicting a level more than levelDb over the line the other's 'nothing audible' allows. A verdict is decisive when there are at least minSegments of them, and the better hypothesis passes at least winnerShare of them and the other at most loserShare.
tolerances.dtxSensitiveNote: Steady signals that Opus DTX can take over, in Steam's encoder or the model's, where the two differ: the tones from 7 kHz up (REFERENCE_2026.md, findings 13 and 14), and the segments the model sends as DTX in 25% or more of the frames of their middle 60% (the 1 kHz sines at -36 and -30 dBFS: 97% and 35%; the 8, 8.5, 11 and 12 kHz tones). Scored apart for Opus hypotheses, in full for CELT.
tolerances.notScoredNote: Alignment markers, one at each end of the signal. Each is the first voice after a long pause (before the signal, or 10 s: pink_quiet_-50dB stays under Steam's gate, then silence_end), so its level depends on the receiver's gain state from before; the controls miss them by up to 1.8 dB.

takes.question: Control: Set B default take, recorded before these predictions.
Does the real engine CELT codec match CELT 0.11 at 22050 Hz / 512 samples / 64-byte packets, and does Steam's voice gate still apply with a legacy codec?

takes.question: 120-byte packets (165 kbps, one public source) or 32-byte packets (the '44 kbps' of Valve's wiki)?
voice_scale above 1: the gain ramp starts at s squared times the target and climbs toward s times it (finding 4), so 2 should push far more samples into the clamp.
voice_avggain 1 normalizes each block's peak (not a mean/peak blend) to full scale: less clipping than the default.
A lower gain cap: quiet segments come up at most 9.5 dB instead of 20 dB.
The output ceiling is int16 full scale times volume (finding 1): at volume 1 the clamp sits at 0 dBFS.
